reasons: every movement triage will ask about has a candidate explanation and none conflict; the explanations are inferred from co-movements, so the cuts below would confirm them

standard.question: What did you change?
standard.answer: ranker_model: lambdamart_v6 -> lambdamart_v7; nothing else differs between arms

standard.question: Is the data trustworthy?
standard.answer: Yes, as far as the checks reach; not checked: pre period

standard.question: Is the effect real, or chance?
standard.answer: Successful Search Rate +0.81% (+0.41% to +1.21%); its interval excludes zero. Across the scorecard 6 of 57 metrics moved clearly; about 2.9 would by chance alone

standard.question: Will it last?
standard.answer: Probably: effect by days since exposure: first days +0.80%, last days +0.82% (trend +0.002% per day)

standard.question: Did the change do what it was built to do?
standard.answer: Not shown. If the scorecard or a cut has a coverage metric (the share of queries whose top results changed), register it as feature_metrics

standard.question: Metric families used:
standard.answer: abandonment = Abandonment Rate, ad_ctr = Ad Click Rate, autocomplete = Autocomplete Acceptance, clicks_per_user = Clicks per User, ctr = CTR, latency = Latency p95 (ms), long_click = Long Click Rate, pagination = Pagination Rate, queries_per_user = Queries per User, reformulation = Reformulation Rate, revenue = Revenue per User, sessions_per_user = Sessions per User, success = Successful Search Rate, time_to_click = Time to First Click (s), zero_result = Zero Result Rate

questions.question: Why did Successful Search Rate rise?
Why did Queries per User fall?

patterns.name: Better results, more satisfied clicks
patterns.label: inferred
patterns.mechanism: The ranking puts better results where users look, so more searches end in a satisfying click.
patterns.source: Kohavi, Tang, Xu 2020, ch. 20 (triggered analysis needs counterfactual logging, and the untriggered complement must look like an A/A)
evidence: Reformulation Rate didn't move clearly (+0.17% (-0.63% to +0.97%))
Abandonment Rate didn't move clearly (+0.10% (-0.50% to +0.70%))
Time to First Click (s) didn't move clearly (-0.02% (-1.02% to +0.98%))

deep_dives.cut: success on triggered queries only (where the ranking actually changed) vs untriggered
deep_dives.confirms: a larger effect on triggered queries, diluted overall
deep_dives.refutes: the same effect on untouched queries, pointing to something other than ranking

deep_dives.cut: success by query class and device
deep_dives.confirms: the gain is largest where the change acts (for example tail queries for a recall change)
deep_dives.refutes: the gain is uniform, which a ranking change rarely produces

patterns.name: A ratio moved because its denominator moved
patterns.label: measured
patterns.mechanism: CTR moved because Queries per User moved (fell 1.90% (-2.60% to -1.20%)), not because Clicks per User changed; the ratio's story is about volume, not quality.
patterns.source: Dmitriev et al., A Dirty Dozen: Twelve Common Metric Interpretation Pitfalls, KDD 2017 (module CTR -40% while clicks +74% and impressions +200%)
evidence: Clicks per User didn't move clearly (+0.10% (-0.70% to +0.90%))
95% of the split comes from Queries per User

deep_dives.cut: Clicks per User and Queries per User per user, side by side
what changed the Queries per User (query volume, sessions, logging of searches)
deep_dives.confirms: a volume or logging change explains it

deep_dives.cut: the same clicks over the finest denominator that doesn't move itself (for example clicks per session)
deep_dives.confirms: the effect disappears on a stable denominator
deep_dives.refutes: the effect holds on a stable denominator

patterns.name: The registered hypothesis
patterns.label: inferred
patterns.mechanism: The new ranker raises the share of searches that end in a successful click.

deep_dives.cut: Successful Search Rate on triggered queries (where the ranking changed) vs untriggered
deep_dives.confirms: a larger effect where the ranking changed
deep_dives.refutes: the same effect on untouched queries

ruled_out.name: More clicks, not more satisfaction
ruled_out.label: inferred
ruled_out.mechanism: Results look more clickable (titles, snippets or positions) but satisfy no more often, so CTR rises without long clicks.
ruled_out.source: Hassan et al., CIKM 2013 (attractive snippets, SAT clicks at 30 s dwell); Dmitriev et al., A Dirty Dozen: Twelve Common Metric Interpretation Pitfalls, KDD 2017 (clicks shift between page elements)
evidence: Long Click Rate didn't move clearly (-0.03% (-0.63% to +0.57%))

deep_dives.cut: SAT clicks (dwell of 30 seconds or more) vs all clicks, by arm
deep_dives.confirms: clicks rise but SAT clicks don't

deep_dives.cut: a similar query issued again within 5 minutes, by arm
config diff of presentation parameters (titles, snippets, thumbnails)
deep_dives.confirms: a presentation parameter differs between arms
deep_dives.refutes: only ranking differs (this doesn't rule it out: ranking can surface such results too)

deep_dives.cut: CTR and long-click rate by result position
deep_dives.confirms: the CTR gain sits in top positions and comes with short clicks
deep_dives.refutes: long clicks rise wherever CTR rises

deep_dives.confirms: element CTR rises while whole-page CTR is flat (clicks moved, not added)
